narrative: This collection agency calls me 4 to 5 times a day, sometimes before 8am, about a payday loan debt. I have asked them multiple times to only contact me by mail and they keep calling anyway. It's gotten to the point where I'm afraid to answer my phone.
extracted_allegations: Collection agency calls 4 to 5 times a day about a payday loan debt | Some calls occur before 8am | Customer asked multiple times to be contacted only by mail and the agency continues to call
policy_cited: 08 General Dispute Handling Process (standard process, outcome classified as partially confirmed); formatted and worded per 10 Prohibited Language and 11 Response Tone and Format
draft_text:
You told us a collection agency is calling you four or five times a day about a payday loan, that some calls come before 8am, and that you've asked more than once to be contacted only by mail. That sounds exhausting and stressful, and we've gone through our records on each point.

How often they call: Our call log shows 4 calls from the agency on March 30 and 5 calls on March 31. That matches what you described.

Calls before 8am: Two of those calls were logged before 8am, one at 7:41 on March 30 and one at 7:55 on March 31. Those are the times as they appear in our log, and we're assuming they're in your local time zone.

Your request for mail-only contact: We couldn't find a record of this request in the account notes or the call log. The only other contact logged is a mailed notice dated March 2 and a call on April 1 at 12:05 that was answered and lasted 2 minutes. There's no note of what was said on that call. Without a record of the request, we can't tell from our records whether calls continued after you made it.

Outcome: Your complaint is partly confirmed. The number of calls and the calls before 8am are confirmed. We were unable to verify that you asked for mail-only contact, so we can't confirm a change to how you're contacted at this time.

Next steps: If you can tell us when and how you asked (for example by phone or in writing) and who you spoke with, we'll review it. You're welcome to send us anything further at any time, including a written request for mail-only contact, and it will be reviewed. You can reply to this message or call the number on your account.

narrative: I set up autopay for this loan six months ago and it worked fine until last month, when my payment was never withdrawn and I was charged a late fee as a result. I have a screenshot of my autopay settings still showing as active.
extracted_allegations: Autopay was set up six months ago and worked fine until last month | Payment was never withdrawn last month | Charged a late fee as a result of the payment not being withdrawn
policy_cited: 06 Fee Waiver and Goodwill Credit Authority, 'When a waiver is NOT appropriate' (transaction history confirms the fee was correctly charged; explain the charge rather than waive it)
draft_text:
You told us your autopay ran smoothly for six months, then last month your payment wasn't taken and a late fee followed. That's frustrating to run into when you were counting on autopay, and we looked closely at the account history.

Here's what we found on each point.

Autopay working until last month: You're right that it worked before. Your $100 payments came out as expected on March 27 and April 27. Our system log then shows autopay was turned off from the mobile app on May 9, and on May 27 there was no active autopay instruction on the account.

The payment not being withdrawn: You're right about this too. The $100 installment due May 27 wasn't taken, and we didn't receive it by the due date.

The late fee: A $25 late fee was charged on June 1. Since autopay was off and no payment came in by the due date, the fee was charged correctly, so we haven't removed it.

We don't have the screenshot you mentioned. Our log doesn't match what it shows, but we'd still like to see it. If you didn't make the May 9 change in the app, or you have anything else that might help, please send it to us at any time and we'll review it. You can reply to this message or call the number on your account.

extracted_allegations: Account is showing as 60 days past due on credit report | Customer states they have never missed a payment on this account | Bank statements show every payment was made on time for the past 18 months
policy_cited: 04 Credit Reporting Disputes (FCRA), investigation timeline and remedy authority (internal transaction records do not support a correction); also 10 Prohibited Language and 11 Response Tone and Format
draft_text:
You told us your account is showing as past due on your credit report, even though you've paid on time for the past 18 months. It's upsetting to see something on your credit report that doesn't match what you know you've done, and we took a careful look at your payment records.

The past-due reporting: We reported your account to the credit bureaus as past due on April 20, 2026.

Your payment history: Our records show that the $140.00 installments due on March 18, 2026 and April 18, 2026 weren't received. We know that's not what you expected to hear, and we're not doubting that you've kept careful track. We're sharing what our own records show. After that, we received $280.00 on May 18, 2026, which covered two installments, and $140.00 on June 18, 2026. Our records now show your account as current.

Your bank statements: We don't have your bank statements on file. If they show the March 18 and April 18 payments leaving your account, please send them to us. We'll review them.

Where this leaves things: Based on the records we have today, we haven't found anything that supports changing what we reported, so no correction has been made. If what you send shows something different, we'll look at it again and let you know what we find.

Next steps: You can reply to this message or call the number on your account to send your statements, or anything else you'd like us to consider, at any time. Credit reporting disputes are reviewed within 30 days, and that can extend to 45 days if you send us additional information. If you're not satisfied with the result, you can ask us to add a statement of your dispute to your credit file. You're also welcome to raise this through any other channel you choose.
